newsitem.title: FRANCE: Donors pledge $560 million to Mozambique for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Donors pledge $560 million to Mozambique for 1997.

text.p: Donor nations pledged about $560 million to Mozambique for 1997 to support its development and reform efforts, the World Bank said on Friday.

Praising the government's reforms of the civil service, regulatory capacity and the commercial code but warning against any slippage in its move to alleviate poverty, donors said they would fully meet Maputo's external financing needs this year.
Participants in a consultative group meeting noted that it would take at least another decade of strong and sustained growth to make a significant dent in poverty.
Mozambique's economy grew 6.4 percent in 1996 and inflation fell to less than 17 percent from 70 percent in 1994, the Bank said.
The 1996 harvest, the largest in 20 years, and a strong industrial recovery after 17 years of civil war that ended in 1992 boosted exports by 30 percent to $225 million, it said.

"Participants recognised that Mozambique's success in 1996 was underpinned by the government's solid macroeconomic management, coupled with one of Africa's largest privatisation programmes," the Bank said.
The donors said their $560 million commitment would consist of 55 percent investments, 28 percent balance of payment support, six percent food aid and 11 percent other programmes.

Mozambique is the world's most aid-dependent country, the World Bank said. Although the proportion of the budget financed by aid fell to 50 percent from 65 percent over the last two years, donors said they were worried by Maputo's high debt burden.

They said Mozambique had to focus on rural development, rebuilding infrastructure, safeguarding the rights of small landholders and boosting the role of women in the local economy in its development efforts.
